title: Cascades, Pine Forests, and Polish Koniks
lead: A park in the heart of Roztocze. Szumy cascades on the Tanew, pine forests, and a herd of Polish Konik horses — descendants of the tarpan.
body:
A Park in the Heart of Roztocze

Roztocze National Park is one of the most beautiful national parks in Poland. It lies in the heart of Roztocze — a land of gentle hills, loess ravines, and pine forests, one of the most charming regions of Poland. The park protects a fragment of this unique landscape, including the most beautiful fragments of the Solska Forest and the surroundings of Zwierzyniec.

The park is famous for the Szumy cascades on the Tanew — picturesque rock steps on the Tanew river, where water falls with a roar, creating white cascades. This is one of the most recognizable places in Roztocze and one of the most photographed places in Poland.

Polish Konik Horses

Roztocze National Park is also home to the Polish Konik horses — small horses descended from the tarpan, the extinct wild European horse. Polish Koniks live in the park in the wild, forming a herd that can be observed from a distance. This is one of the few places in Poland where you can see these animals in their natural environment.

It is also worth visiting Zwierzyniec — a picturesque town where the park's headquarters, the church on the water, and the Echo Ponds, home to many bird species, are located. It is an ideal base for hikes in the park and the surrounding areas.
tip: Bring a bike — Roztocze is a land perfect for cyclists. The routes are well-marked, and the landscapes take your breath away.
